ASR Space Team - Madinah

We are an established team working on an AI-driven, interactive space data solution for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. This team page is created for our registered teammates to join officially.
summary: Satellites have mapped Earth's fires since 2000, but the record is split between MODIS and VIIRS, which cannot be compared directly. Read naively, the record exaggerates burning by over 700% once VIIRS arrives - a "false fire explosion". And MODIS is retiring: Suomi NPP stopped delivering data in November 2026. Fire Calendar harmonizes 25 years of NASA FIRMS hotspots (about 565 million detections) into one consistent record, cutting that error to 2.2% in a blind test. It turns the record into a burning activity calendar anyone can read: Earth's fire rings, drawn like tree rings, plus a weather-style monthly Fire Forecast. For any area on Earth it says whether this season is normal, when the danger season starts and peaks, and how many fires to expect over the next three months, from a machine-learning model whose error is 40% lower than the best simple method. A readiness list ranks the areas that need attention first. Fire Calendar moves civil defense, firefighters and land managers from firefighting to fire-readiness.
details:
THE PROBLEM
Fire managers need two answers every year: when does our fire season start, and is what we see now normal or dangerous? Both depend on comparing today with the past, and NASA's satellite fire record is split. MODIS (Terra 2000, Aqua 2002) detects fires at 1 km. VIIRS (Suomi NPP 2012, NOAA-20 2018) detects them at 375 m and catches far smaller fires: 56% of VIIRS detections are fires too small for MODIS to see. Put side by side, burning appears to explode after 2012 (+718%). The Earth did not change; the camera did. With MODIS near the end of its life and Suomi NPP data delivery stopped in November 2026, 25 years of history risk becoming impossible to compare with the future.

WHAT FIRE CALENDAR DOES
1. Cleans the record. Keeps nominal and high confidence detections and removes gas flares, industry and volcanoes, including sources labelled as vegetation: any ~1 km spot hot in 4+ months of a year, in 3+ years, is treated as a permanent heat source.
2. Makes every year comparable. Terra-only months before 2002 are scaled to Terra+Aqua; VIIRS counts are averaged per satellite, so a new satellite is not a new trend; and two bridges link MODIS and VIIRS, fitted on the years both sensors fly (2012-2025). Physical bridge: VIIRS pixels are merged into 1 km bins per overpass and bins weaker than MODIS can detect are dropped (best cut, 4 MW, chosen from the data). Statistical bridge: a ratio for each 5-degree region and calendar month, shrunk toward the regional value when fires are few, with uncertainty from resampling years.
3. Proves it. We pretend MODIS retired early: the bridges are fitted on 2012-2021 only and rebuild 2022-2025 blind. The bridge reaches R2 = 0.95 (log scale) with a +2.2% total bias; one global ratio reaches 0.92; raw VIIRS read as MODIS reaches 0.25 with a +718% bias.
4. Looks ahead with machine learning. Gradient-boosted trees (Poisson loss for counts, 10/90% quantile models for a range, and a fire / no-fire classifier) forecast every active 25 km cell 1-3 months ahead, using 21 leakage-free features. Tested blind on 2025, a year the model never saw, the Poisson error is 40% lower than the best simple method one month ahead and 29% lower three months ahead; the classifier reaches AUC 0.92. We forecast critical periods, not single ignitions.
5. Reads it for people. Pick any area (a place, a box on the map, or coordinates) and get a weather-style Fire Forecast card (expected fires next month, a risk level, when the season usually ends), an "Is this normal?" sentence, Earth's fire rings with a before/after handle, a month-by-month calendar, season shift, repeat-burn hotspots, weekly human rhythms, and CSV/PNG downloads. A Readiness list ranks the areas that need attention first, and a "When" world map with a Fire wave shows the burning season travelling around the planet.

WHO IT IS FOR
Civil defense and firefighters planning crews and equipment, land managers and afforestation programmes such as the Saudi Green Initiative, health authorities warning before the smoke season, and scientists who need an honest long-term record.

IMPACT
The UN Environment Programme calls on governments to move fire spending from response to prevention and preparedness. Preparedness needs to know when and where, and that needs a record that does not break every time a satellite retires. Fire Calendar works for any area on Earth, needs no expert to read, runs in any browser, in English and Arabic, and is open source: https://github.com/Atheer-Hr/fire-rings

TOOLS
Python (pandas, NumPy, PyArrow, scikit-learn) for the pipeline; a static website with Leaflet and D3, hosted on GitHub Pages.

Pitch deck (7 slides): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/14Bxd80GzpiD_LaJyR6O0FlW714n_gVNR/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=107094360190277248809&rtpof=true&sd=true
